summary: This program converts a single byte (a number from 0 to 255) into its binary representation as a string of 0s and 1s. It does this by checking each bit position from highest to lowest, and builds up the result string one character at a time.

explanations.3: I is the loop counter that will count down through bit positions, and Temp is a temporary variable that will hold the result of checking whether a specific bit is set.
explanations.10: The loop counts down from 7 to 0 because a byte has 8 bits numbered from position 7 (the most significant, leftmost bit) down to position 0 (the least significant, rightmost bit).
explanations.11: The expression (1 shl I) shifts the number 1 left by I positions, creating a mask with only one bit set at position I. Using 'and' with Chiffre isolates that single bit position.
explanations.12: If the bit at position I was 0, Temp will be 0, so we append '0' to the string; otherwise the bit was 1 and we append '1'.
explanations.15: The function returns the complete binary string that was built up in the loop.
